newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol seen brighter after 9-mth earnings.
newsitem.headline: Repsol seen brighter after 9-mth earnings.

text.p: The fall in nine-month earnings at Spanish energy group Repsol SA was roughly in line with market estimates, but a brighter outlook for next year should start to buck up the share price, analysts said on Wednesday.

"The future looks better and (the firm) seems to be starting to recover. The market has to some extent punished (the share price). It could now see a slight recovery," said Javier Borrachero, energy analyst at Central Hispano Bolsa.
Just before the close on Tuesday Repsol posted a 5.6 percent fall in net profit to 86.98 billion pesetas and a 15.3 percent fall in operating profit for the nine months to September.
Earnings were hit by a 67 percent fall in operating profit in the chemicals division.
The figures were slightly below the consensus estimate shown in a Reuter poll of a 3.6 percent fall in net profit.
At 1300 GMT, Repsol was up 15 pesetas, 0.35 percent, to 4,310, while the Ibex-35 index of leading stocks was down 0.04 percent to 4,457.81.
In the results breakdown, Borrachero highlighted burgeoning financial costs because of a high level of investment, both in new purchases and in the chemical and gas divisions.
This was unlikely to see short-term returns but was good for the firm in the longer run, he said.
In the second quarter Repsol bought a controlling 37.7 percent stake in Argentine refinery Astra and formed part of a consortium which bought 60 percent of Peru's La Pampilla refinery.

One Madrid brokerage was expecting improvement from the exploration and production unit in the final quarter of the year due to the start-up of new fields and predicted a recovery in the chemicals division.

"During the final quarter of 1996 we foresee an improvement in chemical activity, as well as larger contributions from exploration and production, thanks to Astra's consolidation and the rise in the price of crude," it said in a note.
An energy analyst at Renta 4 brokerage said that because of the poor chemicals performance, results as a whole were slightly worse than they expected.
"We see a recovery in the fourth quarter, although it may be insufficient to balance out the first nine months," she said.
She agreed the firm should perform better next year, boosting the share price.
"Although short-term the shares could fall a little, results have been discounted and a favourable outlook for next year allows good expectations for the share price."
The government plans to sell its remaining 10 percent stake in Repsol on the bourse early next year.
